ordered_step_reconstruction: With z=(U,P,V,Q) and omega=dU wedge dP-dV wedge dQ, the convention i_(X_H)omega=dH applied to H=(P^2-Q^2)/2+Phi(U^2-mu^2V^2) gives U_t=P, P_t=-rho U, V_t=Q, Q_t=-mu^2 rho V for either relay sign.

At a transverse switch, a=f_+-f_-=(0,-Delta rho U,0,-mu^2 Delta rho V) and n=grad S=(2U,0,-2mu^2V,0). For the signed symplectic matrix Omega, Omega a=-(Delta rho/2)n. Expanding Xi=I+a n^T/(n^T f_-) therefore gives Xi^T Omega Xi=Omega exactly; constant-cell Hamiltonian flows are symplectic as well.

The vector field and switching surface are homogeneous. Differentiating common positive scaling of both initial slopes yields the exact hybrid Jacobi field xi=z; at each switch n^T xi=2S=0, so the saltation update agrees with xi=z.

For eta=partial_q z at fixed mu and fixed physical time, eta(0)=(0,0,0,1), whereas xi(0)=(0,1,0,q). Their signed symplectic pairing is zero initially and hence at L. Since xi(L)=(0,p,0,r), this gives -p eta_U(L)+r eta_V(L)=0.

Simple indexed terminal zeros give the moving-endpoint formulas partial_q T_U^n=-eta_U(L)/p and partial_q T_V^(n+1)=-eta_V(L)/r. Conservation of twice H from the initial to the common terminal point gives p^2-r^2=1-q^2 with the stated sign.

Combining the preceding identities gives partial_q A_n=(p^2-r^2)eta_U/(p r^2)=(1-q^2)eta_U/(p r^2). Because q>1 and p,r are nonzero, this vanishes exactly when both terminal position components of eta vanish.

Time reversal followed by the common magnitude normalization 1/abs(p), with independent harmless orientation signs, gives U_sharp=-sign(p)U(L-t)/abs(p), V_sharp=-sign(r)V(L-t)/abs(p), and q_sharp=abs(r)/abs(p). It preserves mu, sign law, indexed phases, reversed event list, and multiplies both relay integrals by p^(-2).

The energy identity gives q_sharp^2-1=(q^2-1)/p^2. Applying the same transformation twice recovers q and the normalized trajectory, so it is an involution. Since q>1, q_sharp=q iff p^2=1 iff r^2=q^2. At such a fixed point the reflected IVP has the same oriented initial data and, by the accepted cellwise uniqueness through transverse events, coincides with the original trajectory.
